title: Alas, My God! My Sins Are Great
description: Alas, My God! My Sins Are Great in Tonic Solfa to DOMINUS REGIT ME, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Martin Rutilius wrote these words in German. Catherine Winkworth's translation was printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 421.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Eights and Sevens (8.7.8.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to DOMINUS REGIT ME; any other Eights and Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: A-las, my God! my sins are great, My con-science doth up-braid me; And now I_ find that in my_ strait No man hath power to aid_ me.

lines: Alas, my God! my sins are great,
My conscience doth upbraid me;
And now I find that in my strait
No man hath power to aid me.
And fled I hence in my despair
In some lone spot to hide me,
My griefs would still be with me there
And peace still be denied me.
Lord, Thee I seek. I merit naught,
Yet pity and restore me;
Be not Thy wrath, just God, my lot;
Thy Son hath suffered for me.
If pain and woe must follow sin,
Then be my path still rougher.
Here spare me not; if heaven I win,
On earth I gladly suffer.
But curb my heart, forgive my guilt,
Make Thou my patience firmer;
For they must miss the good Thou wilt
Who at Thy chastenings murmur.
Then deal with me as seems Thee best,
Thy grace will help me bear it,
If but at last I see Thy rest
And with my Savior share it.

licence: Public domain: Martin Rutilius died in 1618; Catherine Winkworth died in 1878.
credits: Words by Martin Rutilius (1550–1618), translated by Catherine Winkworth (1827–1878), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to DOMINUS REGIT ME by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
